request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Use fold-level evidence to decide: a config that wins a majority of folds is more trustworthy than one with a higher mean but inconsistent fold performance. Between two configs with similar fold-win rates, prefer the simpler model. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 0 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means one config clearly wins most folds and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means fold wins are split roughly evenly or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. Compare fold-by-fold: count how many folds each config wins to assess which is genuinely better vs lucky. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

concerns: Run 1 wins all 5 folds against both run 2 and run 3 (0.7831 vs 0.7669 vs 0.7396; 0.7304 vs 0.7053 vs 0.6692; 0.6273 vs 0.6142 vs 0.5712; 0.8014 vs 0.7947 vs 0.7676; 0.7312 vs 0.6901 vs 0.6878), so the ranking is consistent across folds.

Fold-to-fold spread is large (SD about 0.07; fold 3 is about 0.63 versus about 0.80 for fold 4), and the gap between run 1 and run 3 (about 0.02 mean) is smaller than that SD. The consistent ordering suggests the folds share difficulty rather than that run 1 is far better.
Only 3 configs were tried, so the search space is barely explored and run 1 may not be near the best achievable.

The PotentialFraud label has an undocumented origin and may reflect investigator suspicion or a rule-based process rather than confirmed fraud. A model may be learning the labelling process, so PR-AUC of about 0.73 and ROC-AUC of about 0.94 should not be read as true fraud detection.

Run 1 uses the 'all' feature set, which includes size features. Provider volume features could act as proxies for the label, so the model may favor large providers. The no_size runs (2 and 3) score lower, which is consistent with that proxy effect, but this is not tested.
Precision at k=50 is similar across runs (0.736-0.772). Run 3 has the highest prec@50 (0.772 vs 0.764), which matters more for a queue of about 100, but the difference is within noise.
Claims span only about 13 months. Temporal drift or leakage across folds is unverified, and the CV may not mirror prospective use.
Run 1 uses no imbalance handling, which is simpler than the class_weight runs, and it still performs best, which is a point in its favor.
